canonical_statement: For every positive natural number n, among exactly 2 * n - 1 integer occurrences there are exactly n selected occurrences whose sum is divisible by n.

source_selection.citation: P. Erdos, A. Ginzburg, and A. Ziv, Theorem in the additive number theory, Bulletin of the Research Council of Israel, Section F, volume 10 F, number 1 (August 1961), pages 41-43
source_selection.observed_statement: Each set of 2n-1 integers contains some subset of n elements the sum of which is a multiple of n.
source_selection.interpretation: The positive n boundary follows the prime/composite proof and ordinary positive-modulus convention. Indexed occurrences in the proof justify Multiset Int, retaining repetitions despite the theorem sentence's set/subset wording.
source_selection.review_boundary: The intake-inspected primary scan supports H1. Independent transcription, positivity and occurrence review, citation pagination, correction and errata review, proof-node mapping, H0 admission, and master acceptance remain open.

domain_and_universes: n : Nat with 0 < n; s t : Multiset Int; the target is a proposition in Lean universe 0.
conclusion: There is t : Multiset Int with t <= s, t.card = n, and (n : Int) dividing t.sum.

encoding_decisions.input_container: Multiset Int represents integer occurrences and retains repeated values without imposing an order or consecutive-subsequence condition.
encoding_decisions.selection: t <= s is the multiset subobject relation, so an occurrence cannot be selected more often than it occurs in s.
encoding_decisions.input_cardinality: Equality to 2 * n - 1 is source-shaped; the stronger at-least-count proposition is only an alternate that implies the root.
encoding_decisions.witness_cardinality: t.card = n requires exactly n selected occurrences.
encoding_decisions.modulus: n is positive in the canonical root and is cast to Int in the divisibility conclusion.
encoding_decisions.sum_condition: (n : Int) divides t.sum; a checked iff relates this to the same integer sum casting to zero in ZMod n.

minimal_import_result: The one direct import supplies ZMod, its integer-cast zero/divisibility theorem, Multiset, integer additive structure, and Multiset.sum. Deleting it makes Multiset unknown. The proof-bearing Mathlib.Combinatorics.Additive.ErdosGinzburgZiv module is not imported.

alternate_encodings.boundary: This is the all-natural, at-least-input-count proposition shape of the pinned mathlib candidate. Only its checked implication to the positive exact-count root is credited; no proof of AtLeastCountTarget is imported or claimed.
The same integer multiset and selected integer submultiset are retained; only divisibility of t.sum is rewritten as its integer cast being zero in ZMod n.

excluded_alternate_encodings: Finset Int, which would erase repeated input values
a consecutive List subsequence or a reordered list without an occurrence-preserving transport
a ZMod-valued input root rather than the source's integer input
a nonempty or at-most-n zero-sum selection
integer sum equal to zero rather than divisible by n
a prime-only or finite-abelian-group theorem used as the root

mutation_tests.method: Lean rejects definitional equality between the canonical target and every mutation; the validator also serializes every fully explicit expression and requires a distinct SHA-256 fingerprint.

degenerate_cases: n = 0 is excluded. n = 1 is included. Repeated, all-equal, zero, and negative input integers are included. The input has exactly 2 * n - 1 occurrences; no distinctness, ordering, connectedness, primality, or nonzero-input premise is added.
